item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Thinking about this….I'm seeing this as one of those songs where the verses are spoken in a quick narrative way (think "Devil goes down to Georgia") with the chorus sung in a simple catchy sounding up/down tune. That would lend itself well to having nothing but drums too.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Constellation Starfish cares little for details. They're all about riding the wave, man, catching the breeze. Sometime that breeze takes them to a concert on the beach, other times on a magical space voyage alongside an interstellar truck driver with a passion for space brew.

Also, Sun Ra wasn't the inspiration for this one. You want to direct your attention to Leo Sayer.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very creative, no question…I just wonder if there's enough detail to really get a sense of the, er, object. I suppose I'm spoiled by all the intricate descriptions of SCPs…

Incidentally, I read this and started thinking of Sun Ra, am I close?

item.content:encoded:
Get someone to actually write you music for the lyrics and you'll be on your way.

By which I mean, music for the vocals. Obviously no music needs to be written for the guitars, and the drums will come naturally once the melody has been established.

item.title: Gotta get that Space Brew
item.content:encoded:
So here's the first track off the Constellation Starfish EP, titled "Old Chilly the Space Trucker". The western fifthists don't have a formal documentation of sorts, so they tend to do all of their documenting through songs and lyrics. This, then, is the documentation of a skip (that doesn't exist, before you go looking) written in the style of Constellation Starfish.

The release party has started! Get those glowsticks out! Woooo!
